checks.text: The page displays the heading "Pixel Art Editor" and a canvas area with a visible grid of 16x16 pixels.

Selecting the "Brush" tool from the toolbar, choosing the color "#FF0000" in the ColorPicker, and clicking the center pixel of the canvas changes that pixel to red; the status bar shows "Pixel (8,8) set to #FF0000".
Clicking the "Add Layer" button creates a new layer named "Layer 2" in the layers panel, which now lists "Layer 1" and "Layer 2" with "Layer 2" selected.
With "Layer 2" selected, drawing a pixel at (1,1) with color "#00FF00" and then switching to "Layer 1" shows the pixel at (1,1) as transparent, while switching back to "Layer 2" shows it as green.
Clicking the "Export PNG" button triggers a download of a file named "sprite.png" with dimensions 16x16 pixels.
Selecting the "Eraser" tool and clicking the red pixel at (8,8) changes that pixel to transparent; the status bar shows "Pixel (8,8) erased".
Typing "#0000FF" in the hex field of the ColorPicker updates the active color to blue, and the RGB fields display "0", "0", "255".
Clicking the "Delete Layer" button while "Layer 2" is selected removes it from the layers panel, leaving only "Layer 1" selected.
Reload keeps the layer named "Layer 1" and the red pixel at (8,8) visible on the canvas after reloading the page.
